title: Creational Dependency Overload (Complex Scaffolding)
pattern: A test setup block that requires assembling a massive, complex object graph (transitive dependencies depending on other dependencies) just to exercise a simple calculation.
why_bad: It points to poor code design: high coupling and responsibility overload in production code [157]. It increases test maintenance costs since any change to an unrelated constructor breaks tests across the entire codebase [203].
detection: The test setup is dominated by constructors and complex object instantiation chains compared to the actual execution step [203].
counterexample: Constructing a complete object graph inside integration tests where actual end-to-end component interaction is the subject of validation.
fix: Refactor production code to extract the decision logic into pure functions that operate on primitive values, decoupled from complex dependency structures [15, 157].
source:
*   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Dependency Construction" (p. 267) [203, 524]
*   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Unit Testing: Thoughtful Design" (p. 213) [157]
*   *Working Effectively with Legacy Code*, "The Case of the Onion Parameter" (p. 120) [311]
